gap: No result ChatGPT got states that no named reviewer or lab has published a measured treat-toss distance, treats-per-toss count, jam rate or app latency for any under-$100 candidate. The closest named finding is WIRED's tester (Molly Higgins, updated 2026-10-24), who reports that the Furbo Mini 360° can't schedule feedings or change how much it dispenses, while the Petcube Bites 2 Lite lets you control both treat amount and toss distance.
standout_why: I compared WIRED's best-pet-cameras gallery (cited in every chat), VettedFur, Good Housekeeping (cited once), HomeGearLab (cited once) and The Consumer's Guide. VettedFur, HomeGearLab and The Consumer's Guide each say on the page that they did not test or measure anything. Good Housekeeping says its Institute lab tested 'more than two dozen' cameras but prints no numbers. WIRED gives only qualitative test notes, such as the Mini 360's fixed dispense amount, its 'jarring, loud chirping noise' and the Tkenpro being 'never laggy'. WIRED is already cited, so those notes are partly available to ChatGPT. What none of the rivals says is that no rival has measured these cameras at all. That absence is the only new point, and it is weak as a page fact.
decides: It confirms the Petcube Bites 2 Lite pick on control, not on measured performance. It is the only under-$100 candidate where a named tester (WIRED) confirms adjustable amount and distance. WIRED says the Mini 360° gives no control over the amount, and the maker lists it only as a 'light snack tossing mechanism'. The page should not claim any measured toss distance or latency, because no named source has measured them for these models.
